title: Example Dental Clinic: main number build plan
subtitle: Draft v1 from the client's replies. Try the simulator to see which path a call takes, then use the build tabs when you configure WMS.

Long Closures.label: Inside a long closure (summer or winter)

say.on: Meeting Mode is on, so the call goes to the meeting message.

openq.title: Open right now?

cases.say: Office Mode is Force In Hours, so the clinic is treated as open regardless of the schedule.
Office Mode is Force Out of Hours, so the after-hours message plays.
The date falls inside a long closure, so the long-closure message with dates plays.
Today is a stat holiday, so the after-hours message plays.

openq.else_say: Inside business hours, so the call continues to the front desk.

ring.title: Ring front desk
ring.pick_label: A free phone is picked up during the ring stage
ring.note: Skipping needs the free-member count jump verified in WMS.

hold.title: Holding message
hold.text: Our team is currently assisting other patients...

queue.title: Waiting queue
queue.count_label: Callers already waiting in the queue
queue.wait_label: Someone answers during the 90 second queue wait

say.next: Meeting message plays, then the caller leaves a voicemail. No press 0 option.
The after-hours or long-closure greeting plays and offers press 0 for urgent concerns.

urgent.title: Call urgent line
urgent.answered_small: Outbound leg uses the CLASSOUND trunk. The caller hears the greeting first, then ringing.

table: Mon 08:00 to 19:00. Tue, Wed, Thu 08:00 to 16:00. Fri 07:00 to 15:00. Sat, Sun and stat holidays closed. No lunch closure.
Urgent contact's cell. Keep it private: never read it out.
Admin A and Admin B [o: Open: confirm names and extensions]
Rings automatically Mon and Thu, with manual override [o: Open: existing login or separate user?]
Inbound routes point at the temporary numbers (a later task moves them to the ported numbers)

list: `Stat Holidays`, full-day dates for the year [o: Open: province, Alberta assumed]
`Long Closures`, one date range per closure [o: Open: dates]
`Laptop Days`, Mon and Thu during business hours
`Office Mode`, 3-state: Follow Schedule, Force In Hours, Force Out of Hours
`Laptop`, 3-state: Follow Schedule, Force On, Force Off [v: Verify: usable in the dialplan]

cols.p: Shared mailbox `Front Desk`, voicemail to email to info@example-clinic.example.

list: `Front Desk Ring`: Call All, members Admin A and Admin B. Call waiting off (default), so a busy phone is skipped and only the free phone rings.
`Front Desk Queue`: same members. Max length 3, announce frequency off, hold music chosen in the dialplan. The group timeout of 90 s is the total wait before the next step.

cols.h3: Sound files (client wording is in the ticket)

list: After-hours message with press 0 for urgent concerns
Long-closure message with MM-DD-YYYY dates, re-recorded for each closure
Hold music: default or the client's own file

cols.p: One Park Orbit, return timeout 45 s, rings back to the parker only. Both desks get a Park Location key and a call pickup key.

steps: If switch `Meeting Mode` is on, go to MEETING.
If `Office Mode` is Force In Hours, go to OPEN.
If `Office Mode` is Force Out of Hours, go to CLOSED.
Verify timetable `Long Closures`. On a match, go to CLOSURE.
Verify timetable `Stat Holidays`. On a match, go to CLOSED.
Verify timetable `Business Hours`. No match goes to CLOSED. A match continues to OPEN.
Jump past the ring stage if `Front Desk Ring` has 0 free members [v: Verify: free-count function, and unregistered phones count as not free]
Call group `Front Desk Ring`, timeout 24 s (about 4 rings). If answered, done. The laptop joins on Mon and Thu.
Call group `Front Desk Queue`: max length 3, hold music, timeout 90 s. A 4th caller falls through to the next step.
**MEETING**: Play sound (meeting message), then Go to voicemail `Front Desk`.
**CLOSURE**: IVR with the long-closure greeting. Option 0 goes to URGENT. No key or timeout goes to voicemail.
**CLOSED**: IVR with the after-hours greeting. Same options as CLOSURE.
**URGENT**: Dial the trunk to the urgent contact's cell, about 25 s. No answer goes to voicemail.

build.note: IVR and urgent dial-out: [v] the IVR accepts 0 during the greeting, and the call class and ACL allow external dial-out to the urgent contact's number. If not, option 0 fails silently.

list: Keys on both desk phones: Office Mode, Meeting Mode, Laptop, Park Location, call pickup, and Line keys.
x-bees Favorites show the switch states, so staff can see which mode is active.
No hold-reminder beep exists. Train staff on park and pickup.
Desk phones lose registration, so the group has no free members. With the free-count jump, callers hear the queue message and wait up to 90 s before voicemail.
[v] Test it. If it's a poor experience, add a jump to voicemail when both members are unavailable.

i: Both desk phones ring together and the first to answer takes the call
One phone busy: only the free phone rings
Both busy: caller hears the queue message and hold music, no position announcements
4th caller goes to voicemail instead of the queue
90 second queue timeout reaches voicemail
Laptop rings automatically on Mon and Thu
Laptop manual Force Off and Force On both work
Evening, Saturday and a stat holiday date play the after-hours message
Press 0 rings the urgent line; no key or no answer goes to voicemail
Long closure plays the dated message with press 0
Meeting Mode plays the meeting message with no press 0
Force In and Force Out work, and the key state is visible on both phones and in x-bees
